To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Nanog is an inhibitor of osteogenic differentiation of committed myogenic cells; (ii) Nanog is a transcription factor that acts at the level of gene transcription; (iii) the inhibition of trans-differentation by Nanog is independent of its role in maintaining ES cell pluripotency.

Nanog does not alter terminal differentiation of committed muscle cells but it is a strong inhibitor of trans-determination towards the osteogenic lineages, which is dependent on de novo activation of gene transcription.
Nanog inhibits the trans-differentiation of myogenic cells into osteogenic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Nanog in regulating the differentiation of committed cells.
the role of Nanog during the trans-differentiation of C2 cells towards the osteoblast lineage and the mechanism by which Nanog exerts its inhibitory function.
the molecular mechanisms that control the balance between self-renewal and differentiation in stem cells and their progeny.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nanog is an inhibitor of osteogenic trans-differentiation.
Nanog is not a general inhibitor of cell differentiation.
Nanog does not directly inhibit terminal muscle differentiation but inhibits trans-differentiation of myogenic cells to the osteogenic lineage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Nanog is an inhibitor of the osteogenic lineage switch of myogenic lineage cells.
Nanog is a key regulator of the balance between the osteogenic and the myogenic lineages.
Nanog acts to inhibit the switch of myocytes towards the osteogenic pathway by blocking the de novo activation of gene transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Nanog inhibits trans-differentiation of committed cells by inhibiting BMP induced activation of gene expression.
Nanog is a master regulator that inhibits the switch to the osteogenic lineage of committed muscle cells and that this inhibition is mediated by a direct effect on the BMP signalling pathway.
Nanog is a master regulator of pluripotency in the ES cells and also inhibits the switch from myogenic to osteogenic lineage.
